newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 5.

text.p: McDonnell Douglas Corp is close to landing an agreement from Deutsche Lufthansa AG to buy as many as 12 of the jet maker's MD-11 cargo jets in a deal that could be valued at $1.3 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.
The German carrier is said to be placing firm orders for five planes valued at about $545 million, and securing future options to buy an additional seven of the three-engine jumbo jets.

A McDonnell spokesman declined to comment on the anticipated MD-11 order. But people familiar with the talks said an agreement could be announced before Britain's Farnborough International Air Show concludes this week.
The newspaper also reported:
* Boeing Co is negotiating agreements with Japanese manufacturers to produce wing parts for its new 747-X superjumbo jets.
* International Business Machines Corp plans to announce its first "network" computer on Thursday as an alternative to personal computers in the workplace.
* Matrix Pharmaceuticals Inc says it is dropping development of a major skin-cancer drug.
* Claridge Hotel & Casino Corp is considering selling or refinancing its sole property, its troubled casino in Atlantic City, N.J., as it faces a cash crunch.
* Kellogg Co sees a 20 percent drop in its earnings in the third quarter.
* AT&T Corp credit card chief resigns.
* Vitalink Pharmacy Services Inc to buy GranCare Inc's pharmacy unit in $370 million deal.
* Observers doubt the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries will hike output amid delay in Iraqi oil sales.
* Senate majority leader Trent Lott douses hopes for passage of Republican tax cut before session ends.
* Rubbermaid Inc to buy Graco Children's Products Inc for $320 million in cash.
* Staples Inc to buy Office Depot Inc in stock swap worth $3.4 billion.
* General Motors Corp sales fell last month.
* Oil prices fall on Iraqi withdrawal.
* Analyst at M.D. Sass Investor Services Inc is accused of defrauding Barclays Bank out of $10 million to $11 million and defrauding his own employer out of another $1.5 million.
* Italian unions make strike threat as Ing. C. Olivetti & C. SpA plans to leave personal computer business.
* PeopleSoft Inc to buy Red Pepper Software for $225 million.
* Campbell Soup Co reports fourth-quarter earnings rise.
* Trans World Airlines Inc says its percentage of seats filled fell in August in wake of crash of Flight 800.
